scope: W5 Work and record-card implementation review; not a human architecture approval
inputAssessment: W5.md and GAP-REGISTER.md describe valid UX problems, but their historical branch, completed-work statements and old test results do not establish the state of this checkout. Rows below are assessed against round27 source and the evidence named here.

rows.detail: One Sections navigation contract, per-chapter section validation, section deep links and post-render route synchronization; Chapter1 brief has its own three milestone steps. Final integrated route checks remain owned by the release runner.

Chapter3 starts at Inputs; Chapters2/3 separate the current comparison question from the shell selection and open on guidance. A canonical record link retains exact identity, including records not drawn as graph nodes. Native quality/decision suites passed; full combined route retest is tracked separately.

Saved latest-action receipts support guarded Undo of supported native input/priority/choice/preference/observation actions. Receipts are actor/revision/state qualified; stale or reused receipts fail. Withdrawal retains observations and history. Prior acceptance or independent approval is not recreated. Chapter7 has Clear draft preference and an unsaved in-place preview. Native HTTP/store tests passed; integrated browser/hosted checks are separate.
Chapter1 has a visible Details affordance beside Edit; the shared card explains how to inspect a record.
Chapter2's visible driver identity uses driverCode; its internal scenario identity remains available to domain logic without masquerading as a second Work record. Native quality suite passed.

Native endpoint pickers are grouped by chapter with current chapter first, searchable, and checked against canonical typed relationship verbs. Invalid existing choices remain visible with a reason rather than being silently replaced. The decorator continues when another chapter's form is absent.

Component-grouped proposed-needs table offers keep selection/keep all and explicit editing; requirements/groups use searchable pickers. Keeping a proposal leaves a draft and does not confirm it. More than twenty simultaneously mounted source pickers now remain operable; selected IDs, including missing source IDs, survive searching.

Shared register summaries and C1/C4-C6 body messages now distinguish an empty register from no search matches and identify the missing record type. C5 source was restored after ENOSPC and syntax checked; final integrated empty-project browser evidence remains release-owned.

All eleven chapters use shared section navigation; C4-C11 use the common heading, intake, register and expanded progress treatment. Intake actions and dialog captions are normalized. Native chapter-specific actions and badge details remain where they carry distinct meaning; identical underlying markup is not required for the shared user contract. Final visual and keyboard checks remain release-owned.
C4/C5 scenario milestone links select the relevant model view and focus the real walkthrough control. No separate fabricated simulation review is added.

Module proposal availability is checked before request and the empty state explains why grouping is unavailable. The complete visual footprint of the module box and toolbar/search width across all viewport sizes has not been separately established by this source review.

Module proposal preflight avoids known impossible requests. Chapter1 Connect controls are disabled with the visible reason Add at least two records before connecting them; the native link dialog independently guards the same prerequisite.

Chapter1 preserves existing record type and hides irrelevant requirement priority/acceptance fields. Chapter5 has a three-field needs editor and shows the same structured Chapter6 needs. Its payload uses native partial updates, retaining exact allocations and unrelated component fields; changed reviewed components return to candidate and changed assumptions lose confirmation. Changed source snapshots display Inputs changed / review needed rather than Reviewed.

The desktop first-visit coach no longer has conflicting left/right positioning: it is bounded in the main workspace, with a separate phone flow layout. Source inspection establishes the correction; final viewport geometry and interaction checks remain release-owned.

Chapter1 rows expose finding status and reference/name/status/findings sorting. Type filtering remains in Context; the requirement and journey sections constrain their type by definition. General bulk owner/acceptance work remains outside this tab repair scope.

Chapter7 Work reuses the canonical choice reading, weights, bounds, dominance and sensitivity. Suggested judgements require an explicit review action. Model-side comparisons route recording into Work instead of silently writing a judgement.

The desktop comparison uses explicit table display, a bounded scroll region and two-column option cards; mobile stays readable. Root's browser evidence must establish 1440x900 with the inspector open.
Chapter7 shows the missing Chapter6 capability prerequisite and prevents opening an impossible realization or empty intake review. No first option is automatically preferred.

Chapter8 Work exposes a nine-row promises table with exact editor-field destinations. Sample checks remain in Work, have four meaningful steps, and require explicit observations before recording. Calculated/model outcomes are not presented as runtime measurements.

Add participant, unsaved proposal wording, empty-library and no-capability reasons, shared intake captions, and the C7-to-C8 obligation distinction are improved. The C7 external-approval action now shows its current architect-selection prerequisite visibly. Specialized source content remains inside the shared Upstream rationale card section. Remaining wording or exact layout consistency must be reported from actual browser evidence, not inferred from historical merge notes.
Chapter7 explicitly describes technology interface obligations and links to Chapter8 contracts without creating a second approved contract.

Canonical interface findings warn when an accountable data owner names a known component/responsibility/contract/party; no identity or accountable person is invented. See validation-gap-register.json.

Plan-scoped standby failure preparation, impossible-plan prerequisites, contextual NOT SAVED Chapter11 evidence proposals, grouped searchable action targets, recovery editor focus and honest blank security/runtime states are documented in output-work-gap-register.json. Its focused continuity test passed; final integrated browser coverage is tracked there and by root.

This Work review did not execute a provider request or establish answer relevance. Ask Sol/Co-design remain the existing governed assistant surfaces; model diagrams remain projections of saved records, not LLM-certified architecture. Final assistant tests and provider limitations must be reported separately.

One record card wraps existing specialized inspectors. It retains native actions and instrument content, derives direct findings/relationships from canonical records, and restores temporary lens state in finally. No record mutation or second record store is introduced. Root's all-chapter record-selection browser pass remains the final evidence.

Exact editor destinations and field focus are present for the newly repaired promise/recovery/cause paths. Every possible finding's editor step has not been exhaustively exercised; the existing 17-check Validate browser run covers the named cause paths, not all domain findings.

recovery.incident: ENOSPC interrupted a source write and emptied public/realisation-ui.js. Publication did not occur during the incident.
recovery.status: Root restored the source, verified 57378 bytes and passed syntax checking; no zero-byte file remained in public at the recovery check.
recovery.limit: Recovery is not a substitute for the final combined regression, build and browser checks.
